expected_value_creation: A separate Discovery Layer will let non-experts and AI agents elicit candidate quality intents through failure-oriented exploration while preserving QIF as the auditable representation layer.
beneficiary: QIF users who lack senior quality engineering expertise, plus maintainers who need a stable boundary between discovery strategy and QIF artifact representation
supporting_evidence: The user design note identifies checklist-driven quality definition as an anti-pattern.
The v0.2.1 consolidation review already recommends package composition and clearer lineage for future pilots.
Existing discovery-session packages capture expert answers after elicitation, but do not define how to choose exploratory strategies dynamically.
success_criteria: The design defines Discovery Layer as outside QIF representation, not merged into QIF core.
Discovery Patterns are strategies for uncovering failure concerns, not mandatory checklist categories.
The design defines dynamic pattern selection, question generation, evidence collection, confidence, and QIF generation boundaries.
The design includes acceptance criteria showing how a non-expert can derive explainable candidate Quality Intents.
